---
title: "Glossary and notation"
description: "Terms and symbols used across the site, with Falconer & Mackay and Fehr equivalents."
---

The two books use slightly different symbols for the same ideas. This site follows Falconer & Mackay for theory pages and Fehr for methods pages, and this table maps between them.

## Notation

| Concept | Falconer & Mackay | Fehr | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Phenotypic, genetic and environmental variance | *V*~P~, *V*~G~, *V*~E~ | σ²~P~, σ²~G~, σ²~e~ | *V* and σ² mean the same thing |
| Additive and dominance variance | *V*~A~, *V*~D~ | σ²~A~, σ²~D~ | |
| Interaction (epistatic) variance | *V*~I~ | σ²~I~ (σ²~AA~, σ²~AD~, …) | |
| Genotype × environment variance | *V*~GE~ | σ²~GL~, σ²~GY~, σ²~GLY~ | Fehr splits G × E by locations and years |
| Narrow-sense heritability | *h*² = *V*~A~ / *V*~P~ | *h*² | Fehr often reports it on an entry-mean basis |
| Broad-sense heritability | *H*² = *V*~G~ / *V*~P~ | *H* or *h*²~B~ | |
| Selection differential | *S* | *S* | |
| Intensity of selection | *i* = *S* / σ~P~ | *k* | standardized selection differential |
| Response to selection | *R* | Δ*G*, *G*~c~ | per cycle; per year divides by cycle length |
| Parental control | (implicit) | *c* | ½ if one parent selected, 1 if both |
| Generation interval | *L* | *y* | years per cycle |
| Inbreeding coefficient | *F* | *F* | |
| Allele frequencies | *p*, *q* | *p*, *q* | |
| Genotypic values | +*a*, *d*, −*a* | *a*, *d* | measured from the homozygote midpoint |
| Average effect of substitution | α | | |

## Terms

**Additive variance.** Variance of breeding values; the part of genetic variance that makes offspring resemble parents and that responds to selection. See [partitioning genetic variance](../quantgen/variance-components.qmd).

**Average effect.** The mean change in value from replacing one allele with another in the population, α = *a* + *d*(*q* − *p*). See [genotypic values](../quantgen/genotypic-values.qmd).

**Backcross.** A cross of a hybrid back to one of its parents, used to transfer a gene into a recurrent parent. See [backcrossing](../cultivar/backcrossing.qmd).

**Breeding value.** The value of an individual judged by the mean value of its progeny; twice the expected deviation of its progeny from the population mean.

**Dominance deviation.** Genotypic value minus breeding value; the part of a genotype's value not passed on through single alleles.

**Effective population size (*N*~e~).** The size of an idealized population that would drift or inbreed at the same rate as the real one.

**Entry mean.** The average of a line or family over all its plots in a trial; the unit breeders usually select on. See [entry-mean heritability](../cultivar/heritability-entry-mean.qmd).

**Genetic drift.** Random change in allele frequency from sampling in finite populations. See [genetic drift](../quantgen/genetic-drift.qmd).

**Heritability.** The proportion of phenotypic variance due to breeding values (narrow sense) or to all genetic effects (broad sense). Specific to a population, an environment and a testing scheme.

**Inbreeding depression.** The decline in mean performance with inbreeding, caused by directional dominance. See [inbreeding depression](../quantgen/inbreeding-depression.qmd).

**Linkage drag.** Unwanted donor DNA carried along with a target gene because it is linked to it.

**Recurrent selection.** Repeated cycles of selection and intermating to improve a population. See [recurrent selection schemes](../cultivar/recurrent-selection.qmd).

**Selection intensity.** The selection differential in phenotypic standard deviations. See [selection intensity](../quantgen/selection-intensity.qmd).

**Single-seed descent.** Advancing one seed per plant each generation to reach homozygosity quickly. See [SSD vs bulk vs pedigree](../cultivar/ssd-bulk-pedigree.qmd).
